newsitem.title: USA: BankAmerica seeks to grow LA presence.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica seeks to grow LA presence.

text.p: BankAmerica Corp chairman and chief executive officer David Coulter said he expects to grow the company's presence in Los Angeles.
"This market is very important to the bank. We will continue to grow our presence here," Coulter said after speaking in a Town Hall luncheon.

Coulter, speaking in his first public Southern California address since taking the helm in January, also said he had bought a residence in L.A. and planned to split his time between L.A. and San Francisco, where BankAmerica is based.
"My wife, Susan, and I intend to be active and involved citizens in Los Angeles, which is why we've purchased a personal residence here," said Coulter.

Earlier, the American Bankers Association reported credit card delinquencies were 3.66 percent of the total number of credit card accounts that were active between April and June, up from 3.53 percent in the first three months of the year.

The credit card delinquency ratio was the highest since the ABA began collecting data in 1974 and it was the seventh straight quarterly increase. The previous peak was in the first quarter of 1991 when it reached 3.34 percent.
"I think banks could be accused of focusing on borrowing rather than saving. I believe saving will be a bigger emphasis in BankAmerica going forward," he said.
"At the national level, today's saving rate is less than one-third the levels in the 1970s and 1980s," he said.
"True to our economic equation, we find that our own low savings rate translates into a smaller rate of investment in our country," he said.
